verses.gurmukhi: ਜਉਪੈ ਜਾਨੈ ਅਨੂਪ ਰੂਪ ਦ੍ਰਿਗਨ ਕੈ ਦੇਖੀਅਤ ਲੋਚਨ ਅਛਤ ਅੰਧ ਕਾਹੇ ਨ ਪੇਖਹੀ ॥
verses.translit_en: jaupai jaanai anoop roop dhiragan kai dhekheeat lochan achhat a(n)dh kaahe na pekhahee ||

en.bdb: If we believe that we see the beauty of the nature because of our eyes, then why can't a blind person who has no eyes, enjoy the same spectacle?

verses.gurmukhi: ਜਉ ਜਾਨੈ ਸਬਦ ਰਸ ਰਸਨਾ ਬਖਾਨੀਅਤ ਜਿਹਬਾ ਅਛਤ ਕਤ ਗੰੁਗ ਨ ਸਰੇਖ ਹੀ ॥
verses.translit_en: jau jaanai sabadh ras rasanaa bakhaaneeat jihabaa achhat kat ga(n)ug na sarekh hee ||

en.bdb: If we believe that we speak sweet words because of our tongue, then why can't a dumb person with his tongue intact speak these words?

verses.gurmukhi: ਜਉਪੈ ਜਾਨੇ ਰਾਗ ਨਾਦ ਸੁਨੀਅਤ ਸ੍ਰਵਨ ਕੈ ਸ੍ਰਵਨ ਸਹਤ ਕਿਉ ਬਹਰੋ ਬਿਸੇਖ ਹੀ ॥
verses.translit_en: jaupai jaane raag naadh suneeat sravan kai sravan sahat kiau baharo bisekh hee ||

en.bdb: If we accept that we hear sweet music because of ears, then why can't a deaf person hear it with his ears intact?

verses.gurmukhi: ਨੈਨ ਜਿਹਵਾ ਸ੍ਰਵਨ ਕੋ ਨ ਕਛੂਐ ਬਸਾਇ ਸਬਦ ਸੁਰਤਿ ਸੋ ਅਲਖ ਲੇਖ ਲੇਖਹੀ ॥੩੫੨॥
verses.translit_en: nain jihavaa sravan ko na kachhooaai basai sabadh surat so alakh lekh lekhahee ||352||

en.bdb: Eyes, tongue and ears have no power of their own; only with words, can they enable us to enjoy what we see, speak or hear. Similarly, engaging with the words of the Guru and meditating on Naam, is it possible to realize and enjoy the Gurus love.
